meta.source: FDIC BankFind Call Report data, computed by Market Intelligence

signals.label: HFS transfer
signals.rule: Held-for-sale rose by at least 0.25% of gross loans in the quarter and stands at least 1.5× the bank's own high of the previous four quarters (so a bank that always runs a mortgage pipeline does not fire every quarter).

signals.label: Realized sale
signals.meaning: A sale closed; a loss is a discount
signals.rule: Net gains or losses on loan sales were non-zero in the quarter, and either a loss, or the bank reported loan-sale gains in at most one of the previous four quarters (so routine mortgage sellers do not fire).

signals.label: CRE charge-off spike
signals.rule: Quarterly CRE net charge-offs reached 0.5% of CRE loans, or at least 0.1% and 3× the bank's own trailing average.

signals.label: Unexplained nonaccrual exit
signals.meaning: Loans left the books another way: likely a note sale
signals.rule: CRE nonaccrual fell, and the roll-forward residual — prior nonaccrual plus prior 90+ past due, less current nonaccrual, charge-offs and the OREO increase — is at least 25% of the prior nonaccrual and 0.1% of CRE loans. Cures and payoffs land here too: a flag, not a dollar estimate.

signals.label: Foreclosure route
signals.rule: CRE OREO rose by at least 0.05% of CRE loans while CRE nonaccrual fell.

signals.label: Modification build
signals.rule: CRE modifications to borrowers in financial difficulty rose by at least 0.1% of CRE loans while CRE past-dues (30–89 and 90+) were flat or falling.

signals.label: CRE runoff
signals.rule: CRE loans fell by more than 2% in the quarter and more than 5% over four quarters, both after adding back net charge-offs (a sustained shrink, not one payoff).

cache.note: Objects are computed by the daily warm-cache job and keyed by the published quarter; they refresh when FDIC publishes and at most weekly otherwise. Consumers should cache responses for at least an hour and need not poll more than daily.
